To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H2O/CO abundance ratio is 1 in shocks of 25 km/s velocity behind which the gas temperature reaches 1300 K.

the water abundances in shock-heated gas are in agreement with the predictions of standard theoretical models for non-dissociative shocks, that the water abundance in the gas behind the shock front increases by about an order of magnitude relative to the abundance behind the precursor, and that the water abundance behind the shock is about 20% higher than the CO abundance.
the water abundances in shocks are consistent with the complete vaporization, in shocks of velocity 25 km s–1, of grain mantles that are assumed to be composed entirely of water ice.

the study of the water abundance in the interstellar medium (ISM), in particular behind interstellar shock fronts.
the study of the chemical composition of the gas and dust in the vicinity of young stars and the study of their interaction with the interstellar medium.
the study of the chemical and physical properties of interstellar molecular clouds, and in particular of the water molecule in the interstellar medium (ISM).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that water is abundant in the gas behind shock fronts.
we have found a good agreement between observations and theory, and that we are confident that the water abundance is indeed high in shock-heated gas.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the water abundance is enhanced by a factor of about 3 in shock-heated gas compared with that in gas at a temperature of 80 K.
Herschel observations of H2O, in combination with previous Spitzer observations of H2 rotational lines, have allowed us to probe the water abundance in shocked interstellar gas.
